current.text: He missed all of last season with a torn ACL. He is now about 18 months past the injury, and one expert calls him fully healthy.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with a knee issue.
He is expected to sit back-to-backs, at least early in the season.
Experts disagree on his early workload. One expects minutes limits and another a slow start. Others expect few restrictions and about 33 minutes a night right away.
Dallas has a league-high 16 back-to-backs. It also has a 4-4-4 schedule in the fantasy playoffs, which one expert calls probably the best in the league.
If he keeps sitting back-to-backs, he could play only 10 games in the fantasy playoffs.
Dallas plays only two games in the matchup week that starts March 1. That is the week before our fantasy playoffs.
Dallas is short on guards and ball handlers. He is the team's main guard and is projected to start.
He is expected to be the second option on offense behind Cooper Flagg.
Experts disagree on a trade. Several say Dallas could trade him. One expert heard no trade talk and thinks Dallas values his play and mentoring more than any trade return.
Experts rate him as a top 15 to top 20 player per game.

Experts agree that his market price, an ADP around 50, is too low, and they want to draft him. The newest call puts him in the middle of the second round. Other recent calls range from the top 25 to around pick 44 because of injury risk.

durable.text: He is 34. He has a long history of knee injuries, including an ACL tear about 18 months ago, and other persistent injuries.
Because of his age and injury history, he will not play a full season.
His best categories are FT%, points and threes. No category is a clear weakness.
